title: Secondary school students’ perspectives on their school food environments and their proposed solutions for improvement: Case study in Northern Benin
content:
by Mélina Maureen Houndolo, Fifali Sam Ulrich Bodjrenou, Waliou Amoussa Hounkpatin, Fadilatou Chabi Yorouba, Hessede Mondoukpe Gbahougbola, Deo Grathias Yevedo Kossa, Irene Mitchodigni, Teresa Borelli, Celine Termote

Background

The food environment within and around schools plays a critical role in shaping secondary school students’ current and future eating behavior, food choices, and perceptions of healthy diets. However, little is known about how secondary school students in low-income settings perceive these environments and how such perceptions may influence their food practices.

Methods

A qualitative study was conducted in the municipalities of Natitingou (urban) and Boukombe (rural), Northern Benin, to explore secondary school students’ perceptions of their school food environments. In each municipality, two focus group discussions were held: one with lower-secondary students (11–15 years), and one with upper-secondary students (14–19 years), ensuring equal gender representation. Discussions addressed the types of foods available within and around schools, students’ food preferences and perceptions, and suggestions for improving their food environments. Data were analyzed thematically.

Results

Students reported access to a wide variety of foods within and near their schools, particularly in urban settings. However, most of these foods were energy-dense and high in sugar, while fruit and vegetables were rarely available. Participants perceived their school food environments as largely unhealthy, citing inadequate food hygiene practices and poor vendor sanitation as major concerns.

Conclusion

Findings highlight the need to integrate secondary school students’ perspectives into efforts to improve school food environments in Benin. Policies promoting the availability of nutritious foods and strengthening hygiene standards in and around schools could support healthier dietary behaviors among students. Future research should examine how these environments and perceptions influence secondary school students’ long-term nutrition and health outcomes.
author: Mélina Maureen Houndolo
